prompt: What does "www" stand for in a web address?
funFact: Its inventor Tim Berners-Lee later said the double-u name was a mistake — nine syllables for three letters.

prompt: What does "AI" stand for?
funFact: The term was coined for a 1956 workshop at Dartmouth College.

prompt: What does "USB" stand for?
funFact: Its designer has said the reversible plug was dropped to halve the cost of the connector.

prompt: What does "PDF" stand for?
funFact: The format was designed so a page would print identically on any machine — the "paper" was the point.

prompt: Which company makes the iPhone?
funFact: The first model could not copy and paste text, and had no app store for its first year.

prompt: What does GPS help a device work out?
funFact: It works by timing signals from satellites, so a receiver needs an extremely accurate clock.

prompt: What does "CPU" stand for?
funFact: Modern ones spend most of their time waiting for memory rather than actually calculating.

prompt: What is the small picture representing an app called?
funFact: The desktop metaphor of files, folders and a trash can came out of Xerox research in the 1970s.

prompt: Which key combination usually copies text?
funFact: Cut, copy and paste sit next to each other on the keyboard for exactly that reason.

prompt: What does "URL" stand for?
funFact: The double slash after the colon serves no purpose; its inventor has publicly apologised for it.

prompt: Which company created ChatGPT?
funFact: Anthropic — maker of Claude — was founded by former OpenAI researchers.

prompt: In which decade was the first email sent?
funFact: Ray Tomlinson sent it in 1971 and picked the @ sign to separate user from machine.

prompt: Which company owns the Android operating system?
funFact: It began as a startup aimed at digital cameras, and was bought for a reported fifty million dollars.

prompt: Which company created the PlayStation?
funFact: It started as a CD add-on for a Nintendo console; the deal collapsed and the add-on became a rival.

prompt: Which company created the Java programming language?
funFact: Oracle owns it now, but only because it bought the company that built it, years after the fact.

prompt: Which social network was started in a Harvard dorm room?
funFact: For its first months you needed a university email address to sign up at all.

prompt: Which company makes the Kindle e-reader?
funFact: The screen is not a screen in the usual sense — it moves physical particles and then switches off.

prompt: In which decade did the World Wide Web open to the public?
funFact: The proposal was written in 1989 and its manager’s only comment was "vague, but exciting".

prompt: Which company sells Photoshop?
funFact: Two brothers wrote it to display greyscale images on a Mac, then licensed it rather than sell it outright.

prompt: Which company made the first commercially successful web browser?
funFact: Its internal codename was Mozilla, which outlived the company and became a browser of its own.

prompt: What was Google originally called?
funFact: The name referred to the "back links" the engine analyzed. It lasted about a year.

prompt: Which AI defeated Go world champion Lee Sedol in 2016?
funFact: Move 37 in game two was so unusual that commentators initially assumed it was a mistake.

prompt: Who is credited with writing the first computer program?
funFact: The machine it was written for was never built, so the program went unrun for over a century.

prompt: Who founded Microsoft with Paul Allen?
funFact: The company was founded in Albuquerque, not Seattle, and moved north four years later.

prompt: In which year did the iPhone first go on sale?
funFact: It shipped with no third-party apps at all; developers were told to write websites instead.

prompt: Who invented the World Wide Web?
funFact: He gave the whole thing away royalty-free, which is the reason anyone could build on it.

prompt: Moore's Law describes the doubling of what?
funFact: It was never a law of physics — it was an observation in a magazine article, later treated as a target.

prompt: Which language was created by Guido van Rossum?
funFact: He wrote it over a Christmas break as a hobby project, and named it after a comedy troupe.

prompt: In which year did IBM's Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov?
funFact: Kasparov had beaten the same machine a year earlier, and demanded a rematch that never happened.

prompt: What is the binary number 1010 in decimal?
funFact: Each place is worth double the one to its right, so 1010 is simply eight plus two.

prompt: The first computer "bug" was literally what, found in the Harvard Mark II?
funFact: The 1947 moth was taped into the logbook with the note "first actual case of bug being found".

prompt: What was the first item ever sold on eBay?
funFact: The founder emailed the buyer to check it was intentional — he collected broken laser pointers.

prompt: What was the first message sent over ARPANET?
funFact: They were typing LOGIN when the system crashed, so the first network message was accidental.

prompt: What was Amazon nearly called instead?
funFact: A lawyer heard it as "cadaver" over the phone, which ended that idea quickly.

prompt: The name "Bluetooth" comes from a…
funFact: The logo is his initials in runes, which is why it looks like nothing else on your phone.

prompt: How many bytes are in a kibibyte?
funFact: The awkward name exists because disk makers count in thousands and operating systems do not.

prompt: The first webcam was pointed at what, in Cambridge?
funFact: Researchers were tired of walking downstairs to find it empty; the pot later sold at auction.

prompt: Which company turned down buying Google for about $1 million?
funFact: Its chief executive thought a search engine that sent people away too fast was bad for business.

prompt: What was the first product Nokia ever made?
funFact: It started as a pulp mill in 1865, and the rubber boots came decades later — those are real too.

prompt: What does the brand name "Wi-Fi" actually stand for?
funFact: A branding firm invented it to echo Hi-Fi; the "wireless fidelity" slogan was bolted on afterwards.
